long.vo: The IPL twenty twenty-seven trade window has already moved fourteen players, in six deals. Here is every one of them.

June, and the first blockbuster. ऋषभ पंत goes back to दिल्ली at fifteen crore, down from the record twenty-seven that लखनऊ paid. कुलदीप यादव goes the other way, at thirteen and a half. Last season, पंत made three hundred and twelve runs, and कुलदीप took ten wickets.
October. टी नटराजन returns to हैदराबाद for five crore, and ज़ीशान अंसारी moves to दिल्ली, for forty lakh. नटराजन took five wickets for दिल्ली last season.
November, and a four-player deal. Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards go to चेन्नई, for six crore and three. ख़लील अहमद and Nathan Ellis go to हैदराबाद, for four point eight crore and two.

The big one. हार्दिक पंड्या goes from मुंबई to पंजाब, and अर्शदीप सिंह comes the other way, for eighteen crore each. मुंबई lose their captain. पंड्या made two hundred and six runs last season, and अर्शदीप took fourteen wickets.
Then, हर्षल पटेल moves from हैदराबाद to गुजरात for four crore, half of what he cost at the auction.
And today. मोहम्मद शमी and एम सिद्धार्थ go to राजस्थान, while Sam Curran goes to लखनऊ. शमी took twelve wickets for लखनऊ last season.
Six deals, fourteen players, and more could still come before the auction on the sixteenth of December, in Goa.

long.description:
IPL 2027 trades: every deal of the trade window so far. Six deals, fourteen players: Rishabh Pant back to Delhi Capitals (INR 15 crore) for Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow Super Giants (INR 13.5 crore); T Natarajan to Sunrisers Hyderabad and Zeeshan Ansari to Delhi; Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards to Chennai Super Kings for Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis to Sunrisers; Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings for Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians (INR 18 crore each); Harshal Patel to Gujarat Titans (INR 4 crore); and Mohammed Shami and M Siddharth to Rajasthan Royals for Sam Curran to Lucknow.

The IPL 2027 auction is on 16 December in Goa. 2026 numbers are from our own archive (Sportmonks ball-by-ball). Fees as announced by the IPL where it published them; the 17 November deal's fees are not stated.
